text:
ana: quick check — uploaded a compact chart mock (throughput req/s + p95 ms) in Figma. space is tiny. do we do dual axis or something else?
li: avoid dual axis if possible. micro unit chips in legend + hover absolute values.
pete: +1. also propose a small overflow badge (top-right) that says "+n" when values exceed display clamp; click opens raw table. keeps canvas small.
ana: accessibility note: hover-only details won't work for screen readers. include a hidden summary paragraph under chart like: "Throughput (requests per second) and 95th percentile latency (milliseconds). Open data table for absolute values."
li: tiny tweak: use full words in SR text (requests per second, milliseconds) but keep abbreviations visually.
pete: outlier handling: cap visuals at 99th pct, mark capped points with subtle outline and dashed cap line. settings: "Show raw extremes" toggle. default: capped.
ana: smoothing should be computed on raw values (rolling median) then rendered over capped points so spikes don't flatten the trend.
li: action items: I'll add unit chips to the legend mock; @pete add overflow badge + cap line; @ana add SR hidden text and tooltip copy.
design-bot: summary: "Prefer capping at 99th pct with overflow badge; avoid dual axis; unit chips + SR summary; smoothing on raw then render on capped visuals; expose toggle for raw extremes."
ana: thanks — will update frames.
